correctness.rationale: From the established product law H_Q=prod G_alpha, derive each small CDF expansion 2ell(alpha)t+o(t) by localizing one exponential endpoint and dominating the other-coordinate integral, with intersection O(t^2). Geometric lower and upper segment-distance estimates yield exactly e^-lambda*t <= survival <= (1+lambda*t)e^-lambda*t and sharp lambda=2/cos(alpha/2); the smallest alpha supplies the slowest tail of the product. Jensen strictness for log ell and the fixed angle sum gives the small-CDF reversal; strict least-angle inequality gives the large-CDF reversal. Full symbolic proof and independently numerical 2D exponential integrals are supplied. No finite simulation is used as proof.

value.rationale: A universal stochastic incomparability theorem for every non-equiangular polygon with at least four vertices, under a natural geometry/approximation sampling model: extreme accuracy favors irregularity but avoiding catastrophic error favors equiangularity. Sharp endpoint coefficients and an exact tail exponent expose distinct geometric signatures (all obtuse angles versus minimum angle), enabling angular inference and illuminating geometric tradeoff; not an arbitrary finite example.
